mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w indicates a renewed return to offices and associated out-of-home activities, which will directly translate to increased foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES maintaining or improving its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating people are spending less time at home, suggests a sustained shift towards out-of-home activities, which will positively impact retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, while RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend from the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The steady improvement in TRANSIT mobility, if it continues to rise above the -55% threshold, signals a critical mass of people returning to public transport for commuting and leisure, which will boost retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility rises above -55% but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in PARKS mobility at t-0w, likely due to unfavorable weather conditions, will divert recreational activities indoors, leading to a compensatory increase in retail and recreation mobility over the next week as people seek alternative entertainment.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility drops by more than 15 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The slight dip in RETAIL_REC at t-0w, following a strong recovery trend from t-3w to t-1w, is a minor fluctuation. The underlying momentum of recovery will reassert itself, leading to an increase in retail and recreation mobility over the next week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains stagnant in the week following t-0w, failing to resume its recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous dip in GROCERY_PHARM and rebound in WORKPLACES at t-0w suggests a shift in daily routines and spending priorities. Reduced essential shopping combined with increased workplace presence will free up time and discretionary budget, driving higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls week-on-week AND WORKPLACES rises week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite GROCERY_PHARM falling and WORKPLACES rising week-on-week at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Despite the recent rebound in WORKPLACES, both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility remain significantly below baseline. This indicates a persistent underlying caution and reduced overall movement, which will continue to suppress discretionary retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining more than 20% below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The overall mobility across most categories (RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) remains substantially below pre-period baseline levels. This indicates a fundamental suppression of activity that will continue to constrain retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks, preventing a significant rebound.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly increases, despite the majority of mobility categories remaining more than 20% below baseline.
